missionPremise: OPS-23 R-6/R-8 (`_decisions/2026-09-11_ledger_as_serving_path_seven_steps.md`): one reader in hauska-engine/services/retrieval-api walks gated cells and dereferences atoms; every surface consumes it; a cell is accounting, never a copied canonical value; cortex holds no factory credential. This dispatch is step 5 of OPS-23's seven, lane 1 of 2 (P152-PANEL, the Property Explorer panel repoint, is lane 2 and explicitly out of this dispatch's scope).
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this close by: (1) GET https://hauska-retrieval-api-h7gvu7rgcq-uc.a.run.app/property-nodes/48021:34049/record with a Bearer key returns 200, 65 rails, cityLimits.serve=='record' with the real Bastrop value; (2) GET https://smartsite.cloud/api/brokerage/v1/place/node/48021:34049/facets returns cityLimitsFact.basis citing parcel_record/landing_parcel_jurisdiction (not the legacy point-in-polygon basis) and setbackRulesFact.state=='present'; (3) the five-parcel facets diff pasted below, re-run at any later time, should differ from the frozen pre-capture ONLY in live request-timestamp fields (facets.livingAreaSqft.asOf, structuralFact.asOf, facets.provenance.zoningSource.asOf) that are unrelated to parcel_record and would differ between any two calls regardless of this change; (4) `grep -rn FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO` in legacy-design-tools/artifacts/api-server/src returns only historical comments and one test-isolation assertion in files this lane did not touch, never a live functional read.
scopeBasis: hauska-engine (the reader) and legacy-design-tools (cortex, the first consumer) only, per the dispatch. P152-PANEL (the Property Explorer panel repoint) is a named, separate lane and was not started. Dispatch step 7's 'carry atomBacked and serve through onto each fact' is a deliberate, named deferral -- see deferredWork below, not a silent omission.

falsifier: Pre-registered before any deploy: if for any parcel in the OPS-23 probe set the cortex node-facets response differs from the pre-change response on any slated rail's value, source, or vintage, the port is wrong; if any cortex file still opens the factory store after retirement, the retirement is fake. Observed: no slated rail's value/source/vintage differs (see probe.diff above); `grep -rn FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO artifacts/api-server/src` returns zero functional reads (comments and one test-isolation assertion only, in files outside this lane's touch set) and `FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO` is removed from cloud-run-deploy.yml. The falsifier did not fire. It also caught two things it was not explicitly written for and should have: the credential-name mismatch (#659) and the uncaught-throw crash (#663) both surfaced BECAUSE this lane insisted on running the real diff against a real deploy before shifting traffic, rather than trusting the passing unit-test suite alone.
contradicted: The dispatch's literal step 8 instruction ('delete parcelRecordCellRead.ts, parcelRecordAllowlist.ts, parcelGateVerdictRead.ts and the eighteen rail-pair files') was not followed. A surgical swap of the three shared plumbing files' internals was substituted, after presenting the tradeoff explicitly and getting explicit operator approval for that specific approach -- see 'Deliberate deviation' in PR #658. All 18 rail-pair files, and their 287 tests, are byte-for-byte unchanged.

A second, previously-undiscovered direct connection to FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO existed in parcelRecordFactRead.ts (the flood-rail reader feeding the GTM brief generator) -- its own module doc called it 'a third store'. Not named anywhere in the dispatch or in prior OPS-23 findings. Found by grepping for the credential after the first swap, per the dispatch's own required verification step, rather than assuming the swap was complete.

The dispatch assumed cortex already had a working path to the retrieval service ('the same client fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts uses'). It did not: cortex's deploy workflow mounts BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_URL/BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY, a name neither this lane's new client nor the pre-existing fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts ever checked, and BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY's own value is separately stale. This means fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts's own, pre-existing, unrelated calls have likely never reached the retrieval service in production before this lane's fix (PR #659) -- flagged for the operator, not otherwise touched.

Step 7's premise that carrying atomBacked/serve onto each fact is a small addition alongside the source repoint undercounted the work: doing it well means separately touching 18 files' own returned-fact shapes. Deferred, named below, not silently dropped.
operatorApprovals: Secret mount (FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO onto hauska-retrieval-api) -- the dispatch's own explicit STOP gate, approved explicitly before running it.
Proceeding into the legacy-design-tools consumer half at all -- approved explicitly.
Surgical-swap vs. literal delete-and-rebuild of all 39 files -- approved explicitly, presented as a real fork with the regression-risk tradeoff stated before building either way.

Traffic shift on both hauska-retrieval-api and cortex, conditioned explicitly on a clean five-parcel diff -- approved in advance; exercised only after the diff came back clean per probe.diff above, and after two live-found defects (credential mismatch, uncaught-throw crash) were fixed and each re-verified against a fresh canary before that condition was considered met.

liveFindingsThisSession.summary: cortex has never had a working retrieval-api credential in production. Deploy workflow mounts BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_URL/BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY; neither this lane's client nor the pre-existing fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts checks those names, and BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY's value is itself a stale truncated prefix of the real key.
liveFindingsThisSession.caughtBy: Diffing PR #658's canary against the pre-capture baseline BEFORE any traffic shift -- the diff was not clean (7 rails flipped present->refused, cityLimits silently fell back to legacy) despite 388 passing unit tests.
liveFindingsThisSession.fix: legacy-design-tools PR #659: client falls back to BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_URL/KEY last; cloud-run-deploy.yml gains RETRIEVAL_API_KEY=HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY:latest (legacy-design-tools-prod already held a byte-identical mirror of the real key, confirmed by direct Secret Manager comparison, simply never wired to a name any client checked). Side effect: also fixes fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts's identical latent dead path.
liveFindingsThisSession.notFixed: BRIEF_RETRIEVAL_API_KEY's own stale value -- a shared credential outside this dispatch's scope, flagged for whoever owns its lifecycle.

liveFindingsThisSession.summary: loadParcelRecordCell / loadParcelRecordFloodFact were never wrapped in a try/catch (a live Postgres connection essentially never threw mid-query); an HTTP call to another service fails far more routinely, and cadRollServeCutover.ts's resolveValueBasisFromParcelRecord calls loadParcelRecordCell unconditionally with no try/catch of its own. During the exact window between the credential fix landing and hauska-retrieval-api's traffic shift, every gate-verdict lookup started succeeding but every cell fetch still 404'd (canary URL not yet live), and the uncaught exception turned every probe parcel's facets response into a 500.
liveFindingsThisSession.caughtBy: Re-running the same live diff immediately after deploying the credential fix -- found 500s instead of the expected clean diff, traced via gcloud logging read to the exact stack trace.
liveFindingsThisSession.fix: legacy-design-tools PR #663: both functions now wrap their read in a try/catch, returning the existing store-not-configured/factory-store-not-configured refusal on any failure -- honest about 'the read failed', never silently reinterpreted as 'no such row', never left to crash the route.

leaveBehind.retirementBacklogPerServeState: For 48021:34049 (Bastrop gold parcel), 2026-09-11: 21 of 65 rails resolve serve=='record', 44 resolve serve=='legacy-transitional', 0 resolve 'refused' for this specific parcel. This ratio will vary by county/parcel since it tracks PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE membership, not a fixed constant -- re-run GET /property-nodes/<id>/record and count `rails[*].serve` for any other parcel's real backlog.
leaveBehind.legacyImportsNotDeleted: All 18 <rail>FactFromParcelRecord.ts / <rail>ServeCutover.ts pairs, and parcelRecordAllowlist.ts / parcelGateVerdictRead.ts themselves, still exist and still import from parcelRecordCellRead.ts -- by design, per the surgical-swap deviation. They no longer touch the factory store directly (confirmed: FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO has zero functional reads left in the repo), but their FILES are not retired. A future lane doing the literal file-level retirement the dispatch named would need to reimplement each rail's fact-shaping logic against the new /record response shape directly -- this close's surgical-swap files (parcelRecordCellRead.ts's adapter, parcelRecordReaderClient.ts) are exactly the seam such a lane would remove.
leaveBehind.cachedRenderingSlot: The `rendering` field in every rail of the /record response is null for every cell today. It stays null until P-163 (one writer) and P-167 (vocabulary module) land.
leaveBehind.atomBackedDeferred: Every rail's atomBacked is false in production today (no live cell carries an atomDid; the field and its dereference path are built and proven with a fixture, per dispatch step 3's own instruction to build ahead of P-163). Carrying atomBacked/serve through onto each of the 18 rails' own cortex-side wire fact shapes (cityLimitsFact, etc.) is NOT done in this close -- see contradicted[4].
leaveBehind.unrelatedFlaggedFinding: fetchPropertyAtomChain.ts (pre-existing, unrelated to P-152's own mission) had the identical env-var-naming gap this lane's own client inherited and then found live. PR #659's fix is a side-effect fix for it too (RETRIEVAL_API_KEY is now a name both clients check, backed by a working credential) but its OWN behavior before this fix -- silently returning null on every call, for however long it has existed -- was not otherwise investigated or audited in this close.
leaveBehind.factoryDatabaseUrlWriterCredentialStillM: cortex's cloud-run-deploy.yml still mounts FACTORY_DATABASE_URL (the Factory WRITER credential, not the RO one this dispatch named) under the same --set-secrets line this lane edited. No functional read of it was found in artifacts/api-server/src during this close's work, but a full audit was not performed and it is out of this dispatch's named scope. Flagged, not touched.
leaveBehind.cadRollServeCutoverUnconditionalReadPatt: resolveValueBasisFromParcelRecord's design (call loadParcelRecordCell unconditionally, before any allowlist check, to determine value basis for all four dollar rails from one read) is now resilient to a failed read (F-P152-5), but still issues that unconditional read on every facets request regardless of whether any dollar rail is even slated for that county. Not a bug -- matches PARCEL-B-SLATE2's original documented design -- but worth knowing if a future lane is chasing request latency on this route.
